FLASHCARD SET · AGES 3–4 YEARS

Color Flashcards for Preschoolers

Twelve color cards with two faces each: a big paint splash with the color word, and a matching picture from real life — a red apple, a blue car, a yellow sun. Name the color, find the picture, then go find the color in your house.

These cards belong to Preschool · Age 3 on the Kiddo School learning path.

HOW TO USE THESE CARDS

Four ways that work.

You do not need a plan or a printer schedule. Pick one idea, try it for two minutes and see what happens.

  1. 01

    One color a day is plenty

    Show the red splash in the morning, find red things all day, and let the set rest. A color that gets a whole day of spotting sticks far better than twelve colors in one sitting.

  2. 02

    Start from the splash, land on the picture

    Say the color at the splash — a pure, unmissable red — then move to the picture card, where the same color sits on a real thing. Splash first, world second, is the whole method.

  3. 03

    Let your child play the teacher

    Hand your child the cards and let them quiz YOU. Getting one wrong on purpose — “is this blue? no, it’s green!” — is the game three-year-olds never tire of.

  4. 04

    Give the color a home

    Tape today’s color card to the fridge at child height. Every trip past the fridge is one more quiet repetition, and repetitions — not sessions — are what make color words stick.

      FLASHCARD · COLORS & COLOR MIXING · AGES 3–4 YEARS

      Red Flashcard for Preschoolers

      Red is usually the first color a child names — it is loud, warm and everywhere: strawberries, fire trucks, stop signs and this big shiny apple. The splash card gives your child the pure color, and the apple gives it something real to hold onto.

      Teaching tips

      What this colour card does

      Names the colour that shouts loudest from any shelf, sock or jam jar.

      Colour hunt

      Today's hunt: count the red things in the kitchen and crown the champion.

      What kids learn from it

      Naming a colour at a glance, before you are close enough to touch.

      How to print it

      Print it first; red always goes first and your child will agree.

      Tip for today

      Keep the hunt to one room today; the whole house can wait.

      Teach it, step by step

      This card belongs to a real class — open the Colors & Color Mixing for 3 Year Olds class on the Learning Path.

      FLASHCARD · COLORS & COLOR MIXING · AGES 3–4 YEARS

      Blue Flashcard for Preschoolers

      Blue is the color of the biggest things your child can see — the sky and the sea — and of small everyday things too: blueberries, jeans and this little blue car. It is a calm color, and an easy one to spot on any walk.

      Teaching tips

      What this colour card does

      Puts a name on the calmest colour in the pack — big skies optional.

      Colour hunt

      Bathroom hunt first: cold tap, toothbrush, sponge — who finds three?

      What kids learn from it

      Grouping by shade: everything blue belongs together, whatever its shape.

      How to print it

      Cool colours pair well; print it next to green on one wall.

      Tip for today

      Ask whether the bath water is blue; big questions start small.

      Teach it, step by step

      FLASHCARD · COLORS & COLOR MIXING · AGES 3–4 YEARS

      Yellow Flashcard for Preschoolers

      Yellow is the color children announce at full volume: the sun, bananas, ducklings and school buses. This card pairs the brightest splash in the set with the sun — the biggest yellow thing there is.

      Teaching tips

      What this colour card does

      Catches the eye first, which is exactly why it teaches so well.

      Colour hunt

      Snack-time hunt: how much yellow is on the plate right now?

      What kids learn from it

      Loud, bright, unmissable: naming the colour that never hides.

      How to print it

      Go double-size for this one; yellow can carry a wall alone.

      Tip for today

      Serve corn or cheese and let the colour be the talking point.

      Teach it, step by step

      FLASHCARD · COLORS & COLOR MIXING · AGES 3–4 YEARS

      Green Flashcard for Preschoolers

      Green is the color of growing things — grass, leaves, broccoli and peas. It is also the color children meet with their whole body: rolling down a grassy hill absolutely counts as green practice.

      Teaching tips

      What this colour card does

      Names the colour that waits outside the back door all year.

      Colour hunt

      Garden or park, collect ten greens by eye alone.

      What kids learn from it

      Careful looking outdoors, where this colour grows on every street.

      How to print it

      Pin it by the window, where the garden will match it.

      Tip for today

      A herb pot on the sill keeps the hunt going between walks.

      Teach it, step by step

      FLASHCARD · COLORS & COLOR MIXING · AGES 3–4 YEARS

      Orange Flashcard for Preschoolers

      Orange is the color named after its own fruit, which makes it the easiest color to teach: hold up an orange and the word does half the work. Carrots, pumpkins and this card’s orange fruit keep it company.

      Teaching tips

      What this colour card does

      Introduces a colour with real presence — warm, loud and hard to miss.

      Colour hunt

      Twilight hunt: count orange things on the way home, streetlights included.

      What kids learn from it

      Recall: naming today's finds again tomorrow from memory.

      How to print it

      Keep it beside yellow and watch the two get confused.

      Tip for today

      If it gets called red, lay the cards together and compare.

      Teach it, step by step

      FLASHCARD · COLORS & COLOR MIXING · AGES 3–4 YEARS

      Purple Flashcard for Preschoolers

      Purple is the rarest color in everyday life — grapes, plums, lavender and the odd flower — which makes spotting one feel like a small treasure hunt. This purple flower is exactly that kind of find.

      Teaching tips

      What this colour card does

      Crowns the set's trickiest colour — uncommon at home, so every find counts.

      Colour hunt

      Colour hunt with grown-up help: check the fridge, the bookshelf, the button tin.

      What kids learn from it

      Persistence: hunting a scarce colour without giving up.

      How to print it

      Small is right for this rare one; keep the card modest.

      Tip for today

      Beetroot at teatime settles the hunt in one gloriously messy stroke.

      Teach it, step by step

      FLASHCARD · COLORS & COLOR MIXING · AGES 3–4 YEARS

      Pink Flashcard for Preschoolers

      Pink is red’s softer twin — piglets, bubblegum, ballet shoes and this friendly flower. Children often meet pink early because so many favorite things come in it, and this card gives the color its proper name.

      Teaching tips

      What this colour card does

      Softens the set with the gentlest colour — and a word children use fondly.

      Colour hunt

      Blossom makes this hunt easy — collect pink sightings on the way to the shops.

      What kids learn from it

      Precision: pink is its own colour, not a shade of red.

      How to print it

      Print two and let a box of crayons finish the decorating.

      Tip for today

      Plasters count, and every house knows where those live.

      Teach it, step by step

      FLASHCARD · COLORS & COLOR MIXING · AGES 3–4 YEARS

      Brown Flashcard for Preschoolers

      Brown is the color of the best cuddles: teddy bears, dogs, chocolate and the crust of fresh bread. It is everywhere once you start looking — which is lucky, because brown is also the color that mixing makes when many colors meet.

      Teaching tips

      What this colour card does

      Celebrates the everyday colour of boxes, baskets and spoons that stir.

      Colour hunt

      Recycling-day hunt: flatten the brown boxes and count the finds.

      What kids learn from it

      Spotting the quiet colours that fill drawers, sheds and cupboards.

      How to print it

      Try printing on a cereal-box flap for full thematic effect.

      Tip for today

      Say the word at bathtime; brown toys surface there in droves.

      Teach it, step by step

      FLASHCARD · COLORS & COLOR MIXING · AGES 3–4 YEARS

      Black Flashcard for Preschoolers

      Black is the color of night, tires, pandas and — on this card — a very handsome cat. Children often love black for its drama: black cats, the night sky, big black boots. This card keeps the drama friendly.

      Teaching tips

      What this colour card does

      Gives the deepest crayon in the tin a fast, confident name.

      Colour hunt

      Check the coat hooks: shoes, boots, one stripy jumper, all black today.

      What kids learn from it

      Contrast: black makes every other colour look louder beside it.

      How to print it

      Save this one for evening printing — dark colours suit the dark.

      Tip for today

      Do shadows count as black, or is that a grey area?

      Teach it, step by step

      FLASHCARD · COLORS & COLOR MIXING · AGES 3–4 YEARS

      White Flashcard for Preschoolers

      White is the color of clouds, milk, snow and clean paper — the color everything starts from. On the splash card it is the quietest member of the set, and the cloud gives it a shape your child sees almost every day.

      Teaching tips

      What this colour card does

      Proves the palest colour is worth naming — sheets, cups and soap all qualify.

      Colour hunt

      Colour hunt in the linen cupboard: white everywhere, and each fold a find.

      What kids learn from it

      Noticing what is missing: white is every colour's day off.

      How to print it

      Ordinary white paper does nicely; the joke is part of it.

      Tip for today

      Whites look different in lamplight; try the hunt again after dark.

      Teach it, step by step

      FLASHCARD · COLORS & COLOR MIXING · AGES 3–4 YEARS

      Gray Flashcard for Preschoolers

      Gray is the color of elephants, rain clouds, pigeons and rainy-day pavements. It is often the color children name last — and then cannot stop finding, because elephants and pigeons are everywhere once you know them.

      Teaching tips

      What this colour card does

      Introduces the in-between colour hiding in squirrels, kerbstones and rainy Tuesdays.

      Colour hunt

      Dull-day special: list every grey thing indoors until the paper is full.

      What kids learn from it

      Accepting the middle colours — a subtle step for sharp eyes.

      How to print it

      Wait for an overcast morning and it will feel tailor-made.

      Tip for today

      Two greys can disagree; both are right, and that is fine.

      Teach it, step by step

      FLASHCARD · COLORS & COLOR MIXING · AGES 3–4 YEARS

      Rainbow Flashcard for Preschoolers

      The grand finale: every color in the set at once. Red, orange, yellow, green, blue and purple, in their famous order. The rainbow splash shows them flowing together, and the picture card shows the real thing in the sky.

      Teaching tips

      What this colour card does

      Bundles every colour learned so far onto one triumphant card.

      Colour hunt

      Grand final hunt: one find per colour, laid out in a proud row.

      What kids learn from it

      Recalling the whole set at once — a memory workout, politely disguised.

      How to print it

      A3 if the printer allows; graduations deserve banners.

      Tip for today

      Cover one stripe and ask which colour went missing; they will know.

      Teach it, step by step
